_comment: Fallback Ambient-AI-style note for Claire, loaded when ?mock=1 is present or when Quo returns no call. Ambient format references: Abridge, Nabla, DeepScribe public sample output.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi, this is Lily, calling on behalf of Test Clinic. Is this Claire?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you have about a minute for your biweekly health check?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you. Please answer the following in your own words. In the past week, have you had any increased shortness of breath and/or hacking cough that limits your normal activities?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I do. I've been coughing up a lot more, and it doesn't look good at all.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I understand. In the past week, have you been taking your medications like your doctor ordered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm not sure if I'm taking the right doses or the right medications. I'm a little confused on that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for letting me know. In the past week, have you felt like you needed medical help, even if you didn't end up asking for help?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yeah. I — I think there was one time where I think I really did need help. I was too much of a hassle. I didn't wanna go to emergency room, but maybe I should have.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me a little more about what's been worse?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: You know, I'm just coughing up a lot more, and it doesn't look great. And I'm, you know, a little bit short of breath when I do activities.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it. Compared to last month, is your general wellness better, worse or the same?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Well, to include last week, it's worse. I mean, I'm not feeling better. So, yeah, I need to be seen.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: In the past month, have you experienced any new or unbearable symptoms that limit your normal activities, such as pain, fever, nausea, diarrhea, or vomiting?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: None of those. I mean, I did — you a little zebraish, but it, it's mainly the my shortness of breath that's bothering me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for sharing that. It sounds like you need to be seen by your care team. We'll now send you a text message so you can take your vital signs on your phone. Please look for the message and follow the instructions when it arrives. It only takes about a minute and helps your care team stay up to date. If you have questions, you can contact Test Clinic at 803-254-5171. Thank you and take care.

note.chiefComplaint: Increased dyspnea on exertion and bilateral ankle edema over the past 7–9 days, with a 3-lb weight gain from the prior week and new orthopnea.
note.hpi: Ms. Henderson is a 77-year-old female with a history of heart failure enrolled in APCM + RPM. She reports progressive shortness of breath when climbing stairs, now limiting her activity after half a flight. Symptoms began approximately 7–9 days ago. She notes mild bilateral ankle swelling in the evenings and a 3-pound weight gain over the last week. She is waking overnight with orthopnea and needing to prop up on pillows. She denies chest pain, palpitations, or new cough. Medication adherence reported as good (furosemide AM) with daughter assisting. Adherence to low-sodium diet reported.
note.reviewOfSystems: CARDIOVASCULAR — positive for DOE and bilateral lower-extremity edema; negative for chest pain and palpitations. PULMONARY — positive for orthopnea; negative for cough and wheeze. GI — appetite intact, denies nausea. NEURO — denies dizziness or syncope. PSYCH — denies depressed mood; PHQ-2 not administered this visit.
note.assessment: Likely early decompensation of chronic heart failure — weight gain, new orthopnea, worsening DOE, and ankle edema are consistent with volume overload. Medication adherence does not appear to be the driver. No red flags (no chest pain, no syncope) but pattern warrants same-day clinical review.
note.plan:
1. Nurse callback within 2 hours to assess need for diuretic dose adjustment vs. same-day clinic visit.
2. Recommend daily AM weight log for next 7 days; alert threshold +2 lb/day or +5 lb/week.
3. Reinforce strict 2g sodium diet and fluid intake guidance.
4. Continue furosemide and lisinopril as prescribed pending nurse review.
5. If symptoms worsen before callback (chest pain, severe SOB at rest, lightheadedness) — instruct patient to call 911.
note.patientEducation: Discussed warning signs of heart failure decompensation. Reviewed daily weight monitoring rationale and when to call. Patient verbalized understanding and agreed to callback.
note.followUp: Nurse callback today (< 2 hours). Next scheduled RPM check-in in 7 days. PCP informed via tasking.

summary.oneLine: Likely early CHF decompensation — 3-lb weight gain, new orthopnea, worsening DOE, mild ankle edema; nurse callback within 2 hours requested.
